name: Ion Exchange - Metal into Zeolite
description: A zeolite or other ion exchanger is stirred in a solution of the metal salt, usually in two or three cycles, then filtered, washed, dried and calcined. The route behind commercial Cu-CHA and Fe-ZSM-5 SCR catalysts and metal-loaded Y and L zeolites.

step_quantities.note: Zeolite suspension in the exchange solution
Filtration and washing after each cycle

source: Perego and Villa, Catalyst preparation methods, Catal. Today 34, 281 (1997); Beale et al., Cu-chabazite as the deployed diesel DeNOx catalyst, Top. Catal. 56, 1441 (2013)
route_note: Two exchange cycles are the default; add a reactor stage per extra cycle. Exchange consumes a stoichiometric excess of salt that leaves with the wash water.
